assessment_summary: I inspected the workspace at /workspace (repo root, checked out at the pinned SHA), verified the toolchain (Node v22.23.3, Bun 1.4.3, npm 10.9.9 at /usr/local/bin), confirmed node_modules and bun.lockb exist, and audited git state: the only modifications are package.json (trustedDependencies block from `bun pm trust`) and the binary bun.lockb — both expected installation artifacts, no source files were altered. I confirmed .env.local was created from .env.local per the guide's Konfiguration section, with MongoDB left at optional placeholders as the guide permits. I verified the dev server process tree (bun dev → next dev --turbopack --port 5173, Next.js 15.4.10) and the log showing '✓ Ready in 2.3s'. I ran live HTTP probes against the guide's advertised URL http://localhost:5173: all primary routes (/ , /certificate, /dashboard, /settings, /imprint, /journey/1, /favicon.ico) returned 200 with real application content (correct page title, full 40 KB journey/station page), and 5 consecutive requests confirmed stability. I investigated the two 500 routes: /metrics fails only because the optional MongoDB URI is a placeholder (guide explicitly states the app works without a database), and /chapter/[id] fails due to an upstream SSR defect (localStorage referenced during server rendering) in a file verified byte-identical to the upstream repository SHA via git diff. Neither is an installation fault. No checks needed to be abandoned; ss/netstat were unavailable but curl success against port 5173 is direct evidence the port is served. Limitation: /metrics cannot be fully exercised without a MongoDB instance (optional per guide), and /chapter/[id] cannot render server-side due to the upstream bug; interactive browser behavior (quizzes, chat simulations) was not exercised but the serving of complete page content confirms the platform is operational. Overall: installation is complete and the software is operational according to the supplied guide.
